hooks.text: Galveston’s weather chief Isaac Cline promised that a major hurricane was impossible.
8,000 people died because one bureaucrat refused to listen to experts.
The US government banned the word hurricane while a monster storm approached.

title: Why Did the US Ignore the 1900 Galveston Hurricane? ⚠️
description: The 1900 Galveston hurricane remains the deadliest natural disaster in US history, fueled by a fatal refusal to listen to expert warnings.

beats.text: Galveston’s weather chief Isaac Cline promised that a major hurricane was impossible.
beats.visual: Portrait of meteorologist Isaac Cline, about 1900.

beats.text: The city felt safe, expecting the storm to curve toward Florida.
beats.visual: Street view of the Strand in Galveston before the 1900 storm.

beats.text: Expert Cuban meteorologists knew the monster was heading straight for Texas.
beats.visual: Belen Observatory in Havana, Cuba, around 1900.

beats.text: Willis Moore blocked their warnings out of professional jealousy.
beats.visual: Willis L. Moore, Director of the US Weather Bureau.

beats.text: Moore even banned the word hurricane to avoid a panic.
beats.visual: Weather map showing the path of the 1900 Galveston hurricane.

beats.text: On September 8, 1900, a fifteen-foot surge swallowed the city.
beats.visual: A 1900 illustration of the storm surge overrunning the city of Galveston.

beats.text: At least 8,000 people perished in America’s deadliest natural disaster.
beats.visual: Wreckage and debris in Galveston after the 1900 hurricane.

beats.text: Many died believing the man who promised a hurricane was impossible.
beats.visual: Portrait of Isaac Cline in later years.

better_than_last: Applied the myth_vs_fact structure to highlight how professional jealousy led to the suppression of vital hurricane warnings.
